readerQuestion: How do I keep a Home Assistant wall tablet usable after idle, restarts and reconnects without confusing a simple dashboard with restricted account access?
directAnswer: Start with a lightweight dashboard and supported Companion app display settings. Use Fully Kiosk for stronger Android display controls, accounting for its paid Remote Admin requirement. Use a separate non-admin account, but do not treat hidden controls or kiosk mode as room-only device authorization. Test the actual tablet before mounting it.
originalContribution: Added an ordered local Fully Kiosk connection walkthrough, actual-entity selection advice, and acceptance checks for idle, reboot, tablet-only Wi-Fi reconnection and overnight behavior. The account checklist demonstrates direct-URL visibility limits without telling readers to unlock doors or disarm alarms.
limitations: Documentation research and browser layout checks only. No physical tablet, battery, Home Assistant permission deployment or Fully Kiosk license was tested. Wake reliability and available settings depend on the installed app and tablet. The access checklist is not a penetration test or proof of room-only authorization.

claimChecks.claim: Hiding a dashboard view tab does not prevent access to its URL.
Administrative and entity operations have separate permission checks; visual dashboard restrictions are not a substitute for authorization.
Home Assistant's Fully Kiosk integration uses local Remote Admin, which requires Fully PLUS or its trial, and exposes display controls.
Companion iOS kiosk settings support display behavior but do not themselves prevent app exit; Guided Access is separate.
